subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-identity mode that receives user-authorized `message.im` events and replies through the configured user token as that Slack user?
rationale: The missing code path is clear, but the permanent behavior changes Slack identity, token selection, and authorization expectations, so automation should not choose this security/product boundary.

options.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a named opt-in mode with live Slack proof, docs, and tests for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while preserving bot-token behavior by default.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Document that Slack user tokens are for read and limited fallback operations, not a supported no-app-badge user impersonation mode.

options.title: Defer for live proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Socket Mode transcript showing user-level envelopes reaching OpenClaw before deciding whether the mode should exist.

recommendation.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a named opt-in mode with live Slack proof, docs, and tests for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while preserving bot-token behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on Slack token/config seams and broader channel runtime boundaries.
